analysis:
Reviewed the head-side excerpts (lines 48119-50176) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. The change is a test fixture: it adds an `additional_context: {enable_thinking: false}` member to some template_input entries (e.g. the tools case at 49157-49159) and regenerates plan/token_ids/chain hashes. It contains no executable code, secrets, credentials, keys, or authorization logic. The visible content is synthetic: fixture-scope, a fixed prompt date, public model IDs, and token arrays. I found no change to TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) or TB-011 (App Attest authorization) behavior, and nothing that touches A-001..A-017 assets.

The only security-adjacent point is the prompt-contract and cache-key consistency covered by T-041: prompt_contract_id values (507d6d7a..., 4b92f730...) and block chain hashes are regenerated. The visible excerpt shows prompt_contract_id unchanged, while the patch shows token counts and chain hashes changed for the fixture case near line 3017, consistent with a template change from enabling non-thinking mode. Whether prompt_contract_id should change when template behavior (additional_context) changes is a question for the producer/consumer implementation, which is not in the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated and the unit text covers only part of the 50k+ line file, so the rest of the fixture and the generating Go/Swift code were not reviewed. Remaining integration question: confirm the Swift/Go prompt-contract implementation treats additional_context as part of the contract/cache identity, so cross-tenant prefix-cache reuse cannot span different template renderings. This is unverified, not a finding.
